title: feat(scripts): census every page key a renderer reads against PageSchema (objectui#9438)
body:
Part of #9438.

Deliberately **not** a closing keyword. This lands the half the card asks for
first — the instrument, named, and shown able to fire — and leaves the half
triage reserved: turning it into an enforcing gate is a new required check and
belongs to the maintainer, not to this card. See "What this does not do".

## Which deliverable this is

The card separates two things. Both are answered here, and one of them turned
out not to be empty:

- **The walk** — nothing checked a renderer's page-key reads against
  `PageSchema` at all. That is what this PR builds.
- **The instance** — the card records zero live instances, both having been
  retired. ⚠️ **That premise is now false.** The first run of the census over
  `main` reports **two live reads of page keys `PageSchema` refuses**, in two
  files, neither of them one the card names. They are reported below and
  **not repaired here** — each is a renderer behaviour change with its own
  question, and this card asked for prevention.

Clause-② stays **`no`**: nothing is added to `PageSchema`, no acceptance set
is widened, no published package source changes. The diff is
`scripts/page-key-read-census.mjs`, its pins, and one `package.json` script row.

## The asymmetry

`PageSchema` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`) is a `strictObject` — the opposite of
`BaseSchema`, which is `.passthrough()` and KEEPS what it does not judge. A key
`PageSchema` does not declare is a **hard parse error**, so a renderer reading
such a key off authored metadata is documenting an affordance **no author can
ever reach**: the page carrying it never parses, the read yields `undefined` on
every page that does, and the dead branch reads as a feature.

## The instrument, stated

The card's first ask is *which instrument a gate would read*. Two halves,
neither of them a list written down in the script:

| half | what it is |
|---|---|
| **ORACLE** | `PageSchema` at runtime, by `safeParse`, one key at a time. The schema's own answer is the verdict: `declared`, `alias` (refused, and the schema names the canonical key), or `refused`. ⛔ Not `Object.keys(PageSchema.shape)` against a hand-kept list — asking the schema is what survives a spec bump, a new alias, or a retirement. |
| **POPULATION** | every property read on a value that flows from the page metadata cache, walked syntactically (TypeScript parser, no type checker) from ONE declared seam: `useMetadata()`'s `pages` member. |

### Why not a grep, and why not the type checker — both measured

A **grep** cannot find the population. `git grep '\.pages'` over the package
sources returns `usePageAssignment.ts` and nothing else; `PageView.tsx` reaches
the same cache slot through `const { pages } = useMetadata()`, which contains
no `.pages` text at all. A grep that misses a root misses every read downstream
of it and reports the miss as a clean zero.

The **type checker** cannot see it either, and this is the sharper half: both
retired instances were written through a type escape — `usePageAssignment`
declares `pages: any[]` and returns `page: any | null`, and the
`RecordDetailView` read was spelled with an `as any` cast before the optional
chain. A checker-driven walk over "expressions whose type is the spec's page
type" finds neither, and would not find them after the spec's types improve,
because the escape is on the **value**. What survives the escape is the
**seam**: the cache member stays declared where the value it yields is `any`.
So the census anchors on the seam and looks THROUGH casts rather than at them.

## Demonstrated before it was trusted

The card is explicit that a gate authored against zero instances needs its own
ablation. Both retired reads are restored — as pins, and once against the real
tree.

**1. Against the real tree, in memory.** Re-introducing the exact retired line
into `RecordDetailView.tsx` (in memory — nothing written to disk) and running
the census over the real source set, before and after:

```
BEFORE reads in RecordDetailView: []
AFTER  reads in RecordDetailView: [{
  "file": "packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx",
  "line": 389, "key": "disableDiscussion",
  "text": "(effectivePage as any)?.disableDiscussion"
}]
```

That leg crosses a package boundary (`@object-ui/react` to
`@object-ui/app-shell`), a destructure, a `||` alias and a cast — the real
route, not a model of it.

**2. As pins**, in `scripts/__tests__/page-key-read-census.test.ts`. Every
specimen is paired with a **control that differs in one word**: the same read,
through the same route, on a key `PageSchema` declares. A green is then a
measurement rather than an absence.

- `priority` sorted off a filtered candidate → **refused**;
  `isDefault` sorted identically → **quiet**, and the read is still seen.
- `disableDiscussion` behind `as any` across the package boundary →
  **refused**; `isDefault` down the identical route → **quiet**.
- the nonsense-key control in the same position → **refused**, so the oracle
  discriminates.
- the boundaries the header claims are asserted too, each with a positive leg
  in the same file so a quiet result cannot be a walk that never arrived.

16 pins, all passing.

## ⚠️ What the first run found: two LIVE reads on `main`

```
context   [REFUSED]        packages/app-shell/src/views/PageView.tsx:132
                           (page as any).context
pageType  [ALIAS -> type]  packages/react/src/hooks/usePageAssignment.ts:131
                           p.pageType
```

Neither is repaired here.

- **`context`** — `PageView` spreads `(page as any).context` into the node it
  hands `SchemaRenderer`. `PageSchema` refuses `context`, so every parsing page
  spreads `undefined`, and the key reads as page-level author-supplied context
  that no author can supply.
- **`pageType`** — the record discriminator reads `p.pageType` before falling
  back to `p.type`. `PageSchema` refuses `pageType` **and names the canonical
  key**: it is one of the schema's declared aliases, mapping to `type`. The
  fallback is what actually decides, so the behaviour is right and the first
  operand is unreachable — and a comment beside it currently says the
  designer-side spelling is "still expressible in raw metadata", which the
  schema contradicts.

Both are renderer behaviour changes with their own question (what, if anything,
should happen for metadata that never passed `PageSchema`), which is why they
are reported rather than folded in.

## Report-only, and what keeps it that way

`census:*`, not `check:*`. In this tree that spelling already means "runnable,
reported, not blocking" — the sibling census documents the measurement behind
that convention — and a `check:*` name invites the next sweep to wire it into a
workflow. Findings never set the exit code. Nothing is added to any workflow.

The one nonzero exit is **instrument integrity**: if the seam moves and the
census finds no roots at all, it would report zero reads, which renders exactly
like a clean tree. That reading is refused rather than printed.

## What this does not do

- **It does not enforce.** Triage drew that line on the card: a reporting scan
  is this card's to deliver; an enforcing gate is a new required check and goes
  back to the maintainer. That decision is what keeps #9438 open.
- **It does not judge page NODES.** `PageNodeSchema` is objectui's
  component-node schema — derived from `PageSchema`'s fields but with its own
  (`pageType` is the node's page-kind discriminator) and `BaseSchema`'s
  passthrough underneath. `PageView` deliberately maps metadata into a node
  before rendering. That side has a different oracle and is a different card.
- **It does not follow a value into an ordinary function call**, judge a key
  reached without being named (a spread, a computed access), or resolve scopes:
  taint is by identifier name within a file. Each boundary is stated in the
  script header and asserted in the pins.
- **It does not answer the mirror question** — a DECLARED key nothing reads.
  `isDefault` is declared and nothing consults it; that belongs to the
  `ComponentPropsMap` declared-versus-read family.

## Verification

```
node scripts/page-key-read-census.mjs --list
  -> 1450 source files, 24 declared keys, controls green,
     11 reads in 3 files, 2 keys PageSchema refuses, exit 0

pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/page-key-read-census.test.ts
  -> 16 passed
```

## Acceptance notes

- The `pageType` comment in `usePageAssignment.ts` asserts a metadata spelling
  the installed spec pin refuses. Noted, not filed — it travels with whichever
  card takes the `pageType` read above.
